answer: Reputation decay curve. Each identity starts at zero trust and must accumulate verified interactions; trust decays exponentially with inactivity, so dormant puppets lose weight before they can act together. A walnut-sized seed score gains only through distinct counterparties, and repeated coordination leaves a pigment-like trace flagged by clustering analysis. Attackers must fund sustained, diverse activity across every vine of the graph, paying continuous compute and counterparty fees per identity rather than a one-time entry cost.
